review_notes: Inspected the entire target (201 lines) with Read, plus the closest analogues Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Interval.lean and Mathlib/Data/Finset/Finsupp.lean, and checked the API used (`notMem_support_iff`, `notMem_mono`, `zero_mem_zero`, `mem_dfinsupp_iff_of_support_subset`) by Grep. Reviewed every proof-bearing declaration: `Finset.dfinsupp` (well-formedness of the map embedding), `card_dfinsupp`, `mem_dfinsupp_iff`, `mem_dfinsupp_iff_of_support_subset`, `DFinsupp.singleton` (support' field), `DFinsupp.rangeIcc` (support' field), `rangeIcc_apply`, `mem_rangeIcc_apply_iff`, `support_rangeIcc_subset`, `mem_pi`, `card_pi`, `instLocallyFiniteOrder`, `Icc_eq`, `card_Icc/card_Ico/card_Ioc/card_Ioo`, `card_uIcc`, `card_Iic`, `card_Iio`. The only borderline repetition I found is the support/zero reasoning: the `support'` field of `rangeIcc` (lines 101-109) and `support_rangeIcc_subset` (lines 116-123) both deduce `f x = 0` and `g x = 0` from `x` lying outside the relevant finite support and then close with `Icc_self`. This does not meet the rubric's bar: (a) the two derivations run over different data (a multiset sum `fs.1 + gs.1` with `Multiset.le_add_right/left` versus the `Finset.support` union with `subset_union_left/right`), so no lemma can factor that part; (b) the only genuinely shareable residue is a one-line calculation `Icc 0 0 = {0}` (equivalently `0 ∈ ({0} : Finset _)`), already available as `Icc_self`/`zero_mem_zero`, i.e. a thin rename; and (c) a lemma stated in terms of `f.rangeIcc g` cannot be used inside the very definition of `rangeIcc`, because that definition precedes any such lemma and the untouchable section `BundledIcc` (lines 93-125) deliberately carries no `[DecidableEq ι]`, so `Finset.support`-style statements are unavailable there. The remaining repeated shapes (`card_Ico`/`card_Ioc`/`card_Ioo` rewriting through `card_Icc`, `mem_pi` from `mem_dfinsupp_iff_of_support_subset`, `mem_rangeIcc_apply_iff` from `mem_Icc`) are one-line wrappers around existing API, which the rubric explicitly excludes. The file also mirrors the existing `Finsupp`/`Finset.Finsupp` interval API, so the parallel structure is an intentional design choice rather than duplicated machinery. No untested replacement is claimed. Remaining uncertainty: whether any automated normalization (`convert!`/`simp_rw` interplay) could be shared across `rangeIcc`'s field and `support_rangeIcc_subset`; no such shared lemma could be used at both sites without restructuring the definition, so I did not report it.
